items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls, so the program re-sends everything: the original input, the model's own reply and the tool result. Picking a or d shows the idea that the model remembers earlier steps on its own; c forgets that the reply is part of the history.
Call 2 input = 1,000 + 50 + 300 = 1,350. Call 3 input = 1,350 + 40 + 200 = 1,590. An answer of 240 or 200 counts only the newest pieces, as if earlier tokens were not re-sent.

Retrieval fetches only the few chunks that answer the question, so each call carries a small amount of text. Pasting 2 million tokens (a) repeats that cost in every call, and a summary (b) loses the detail the student needs.

items.answer: Each session starts with an empty window; the program must save the preferences (a note) and load them into the next session.
accepted: the window is wiped between sessions; save a note and read it back
nothing is kept between sessions unless the program stores it and loads it
the model has no memory of the last session; the program has to save the info to a file and load it next time
items.rationale: The window holds only this session's text. Memory is a file or record outside the window that the program writes and reads back. An answer saying the model learned or remembered by itself shows that misconception.

A fact that can change, such as training status, belongs in the system that owns it, so look it up. A note can be stale (a), deleting it does not check anything (b), and the student's word is not the record (c).
